title: gatedloop project manifest (.gates.yaml)
description: The single project-specific file gatedloop reads. Binds a project's stack to the workflow's abstract contract: gates (abstract name -> command) and surfaces (glob -> rules + live-check).

gateSpec.description: A gate/live-check value: either a literal command string, or a mapping with a required 'run' command and an optional 'requires' precondition command. When 'requires' is declared, the shim runs it first -- its non-zero exit is a distinct, machine-readable outcome (reserved exit code 75) and the 'run' body is never executed.

run.description: The command the workflow runs and reads the exit code of.

requires.description: Optional precondition command. Must exit 0 before 'run' executes; a non-zero exit means the environment was absent, not that the gate failed.

gatesVersion.description: Manifest schema version. Bump when the shim's expected shape changes.

taskSource.description: The spec/task system the workflow wraps. v1 supports openspec only.

gates.description: Abstract capability name -> literal command or {run, requires} mapping. The workflow runs the NAME via `gates run <name>` and reads the exit code; it never inspects the body.

unit.description: Fast inner-loop unit tests (optional but recommended).

ci.description: REQUIRED aggregate pre-commit oracle — one exit code.

eval.description: Advisory eval. May contain {dataset} and {score} placeholders substituted from `gates run eval <dataset> <score>`.

confirm.description: Optional live confirmation of the merged tree, run by `gates merge` step 5 before anything is pushed: the project's own 'bring it up and smoke it' recipe. Red (or exit 75) stops the merge unpublished; undeclared, the step is skipped with a note.

surfaces.description: The changed-file set decides which surfaces are 'hot'; each hot surface contributes its rules to the review scope and its live-check to the live self-check.

match.description: A glob, or list of globs, matched against changed file paths (relative to repo root).

rules.description: Convention rules for this surface. Each entry is a rule-id (resolved against conventions.rules-doc) OR inline rule prose.

live-check.description: Command (or {run, requires} mapping) run as the live self-check when this surface is hot (optional; omit for surfaces with no runtime probe).

gates.description: Optional per-surface overrides for the `ci`/`unit` gates (scale-gate-cost D1). Selected err-full: the scoped command runs only when this is the one non-catch-all hot surface in the diff and it declares the override for that gate; every other case runs the globally declared gate. Each named gate must also be declared globally. Each value takes the same scalar-or-{run, requires} shape as a top-level gate.

conventions.description: Where the prose behind rule-ids lives.

rules-doc.description: Path (repo-relative) to the canonical conventions doc. rule-ids in surfaces are resolved here.

integration.description: How a change reaches main, as onboarding asked and the adopter confirmed (onboarding-asks-first §5). Optional: absence means today's behavior, a local squash-merge at change completion. `gates merge` and `gates integration` read it.

mode.description: local-squash-merge: `gates merge` squash-merges directly at change completion (today's behavior). pull-request: `gates merge` proves the head, pushes the branch, publishes `gatedloop/*` commit statuses and opens or updates a PR; the forge merges it, and `gates record-merged` records it.

requireApproval.description: Only meaningful when mode is pull-request: whether a human review approves the merge. true: `gates merge` opens the PR and leaves auto-merge off. false: it enables squash auto-merge when any declared acceptance is satisfied.

discipline.description: OpenSpec git-discipline knobs (worktree-native-loop design D3). Optional: absence means today's behavior.

propose-branches.description: Additional branch-name globs (fnmatch) accepted for proposal authoring, alongside the merge target (always accepted). Declaring this list REPLACES the default `plan/*` pattern rather than appending to it -- an adopter who wants both lists both. Every non-target branch, declared or default, must still share history with the merge target.

agent-env.description: Environment variable names whose presence (a non-empty value) marks an agent session (git-layer-enforcement D1). The git-layer `pre-commit` and `pre-push` hooks enforce when any is set and are a transparent no-op otherwise; `gates discipline agent-session` makes that decision. Declaring this list REPLACES the default. An adopter running the loop on a host other than Claude Code adds that host's variable.

concurrency.description: Machine-wide gate serialization across every worktree of the repository (worktree-native-loop design D6). Optional: absence means no locking, today's behavior.

serialize.description: Gate names (must already be declared under `gates`, or `live-check`) that `gates run` serializes machine-wide with a stdlib file lock held only around the gate command.

max-wait-seconds.description: How long `gates run` waits for a serialized gate's lock before giving up (lock-and-ledger-hygiene D2). On timeout it exits 75 with a message beginning `gatedloop: lock busy`, never running the gate, and writes a ledger row with `precondition: lock-busy`. Default 480: below the host's 600 s tool-call cap, so the wait never gets the gate backgrounded.

merge-wait-seconds.description: How long `gates merge` waits for a serialized gate's lock at its step 3 (`ci`) and step 5 (`confirm`) (merge-lane-friction D3). The waiting merge holds priority, so other waiters let it take the lock next and its wait is at most the run in progress. Defaults to `max-wait-seconds`; raise it alone when the project's full `ci` outlasts the general bound. On timeout the merge exits 75 and reports the step as not run.

approval.description: The declared plan-approval policy (solo-approval-mode D1). Optional: absence means today's behavior, `review` -- a second party approves via the forge. Read only by the attestation writers (`gates approval attest --local`/`--pr`); the D10 implementation gate itself never reads this block, only the approval keys it produced.

plan.description: review: a second party approves via a PR's APPROVED review (default). self: standing self-approval -- `gates approval attest --local` becomes a legitimate writer.

acceptance.description: The declared acceptance policy for the increment after the loop (acceptance-gate D1). Optional: absence means no acceptance is required anywhere and the merge gate behaves exactly as before. review: a second party accepts via the implementation PR's APPROVED review, recorded with `gates acceptance attest <change> --pr <n>` -- requires `integration.mode: pull-request` (`gates validate` rejects it otherwise; JSON Schema cannot express that cross-block rule). self: standing self-acceptance -- `gates acceptance attest <change> --local` becomes a legitimate writer. Once declared, the merge gate requires an `accept` ledger row pinning the incoming tree.

loop.description: Knobs for the loop itself (split-test-author design D6). Optional: absence means every default below.

test-author.description: Who authors a change's failing tests, in the authoring phase before its first task. separate (default): a test-author agent, dispatched by whoever dispatches the implementer; an implementer with no handoff halts with `missing-oracle`. inline: the implementer runs the authoring phase itself, into the same holding area, bound by the same lock.

attempts.description: Failed attempts allowed per task, per context (retry-budget design D1, D5): red `unit` or `ci` runs after the task's RED run and since its last restart, counted from the ledger. Exit 75 never counts. Once reached, `gates run unit|ci` for the task refuses with exit 1. 0 is legal but `gates validate` warns.

fresh-restarts.description: Fresh restarts allowed per task (retry-budget design D4): `gates attempt restart <task>` resets the failed-attempt count this many times, from a clean tree, in a new agent context. 0 disables restarts.

token-budget.description: Tokens a change may spend, counted from its recorded `usage` rows (token-ledger design D5): input, output, cache-read and cache-write across every model. Optional, no default: absent, no budget applies. Once the recorded total reaches it, task-bearing `gates run unit|ci` refuses with exit 1 and names `gates halt record budget`. The task in flight is counted at its commit or the session stop, so the refusal lags by at most that.

economics.description: Prices for `gates stats --cost` (token-ledger design D4): the adopter's binding, as a gate body is. Optional: absent, `--cost` prints tokens only and says no prices are declared. The shim ships no price list and checks the shape only, never the model names.

currency.description: The one currency every price is in (e.g. USD). Required when `prices` is declared.

prices.description: Model name, as usage rows record it -> its prices per million tokens. A recorded model with no entry is named by `--cost` with its tokens, beside the priced subtotal.

acceptance.description: Where the project's acceptance scenarios live (acceptance-gate D5) -- the only thing the shim knows about acceptance artifacts. `gates acceptance brief` marks a spec scenario `covered` when a line in a matched file carries a scenario marker (`Scenario:`, `Scenario Outline:`, `#### Scenario:`, `- Scenario:`) followed by the same title, compared case-insensitively; otherwise `check by hand`. Optional: absent, every scenario is `check by hand`.

match.description: A glob (repo-relative, same syntax as a surface's `match`) naming the files that hold acceptance scenarios, e.g. `features/**/*.feature`.
